parts.text: Suzie is a big fan of fruit-flavored gum.
During her last visit to the store, she bought four packs of gum.
She picked up two packs of her favorite flavor, strawberry, and also bought a pack of grape gum for $2.
She also decided to try a new flavor, green apple, and paid half the price of the grape gum for a smaller pack.
In the midst of her shopping, she also bought a bottle of water for $1, which she drank while shopping.
Despite the cost of the water, if she paid a total of $7 for the gum alone, how many dollars did each pack of strawberry gum cost?

parts.text: An instructor utilizes a chalk measuring 5 inches to jot down mathematical equations on a blackboard for his pupils.
The instructor is keen on preserving chalk, hence he aims to use only a fifth of the chalk daily.
However, when the chalk's length falls below 2 inches, it becomes too small to write with and he recycles it.
On a particular Monday, the instructor started with a fresh piece of chalk.
His pupils required additional assistance that day, leading him to write more than usual and he consumed 45% of the chalk by the day's end.
If the instructor reverts to using only a fifth of the chalk each day, how many days will pass before he needs to recycle this piece of chalk?

parts.text: There are three trees in Eddy's backyard.
The shortest tree has a height of 60 feet, and the second tree has a height of 50 feet more than the shortest tree.
The height of the tallest tree is twice the height of the two trees combined.
How tall is the tallest tree?

parts.text: Meredith is a freelance blogger who writes about health topics and submits to clients each day as her permanent job.
A blog article takes an average of 4 hours to research and write about.

Last week, she wrote 5 articles on Monday and 2/5 times more articles on Tuesday than on Monday.If she spent a total of 104 hours writing articles in the three days, how many times as many articles did she write on Wednesday as she did on Tuesday?

parts.text: Ellen is on a diet.
She eats two carrots, a salad, and a yogurt every day.
The salad costs her $6.8, while the yogurt is half the price.
How much does Ellen pay for one carrot every day when in total she pays $11.8 for her goods?
